source.prompt: A Pacific wren (Troglodytes pacificus), a tiny round dark brown songbird about 10 cm long, NOT a sparrow, NOT a mouse. One adult standing on the ground, side-on pose, body round like a ball, a very short stubby tail cocked straight up, a thin short slightly downcurved bill, a short neck, thin pale pinkish-brown legs, three toes forward and one back. Dark rufous-brown all over with fine black barring on the wings, tail and flanks, a faint pale buff eyebrow. Wings folded tight against the body. No base, no perch. Game-ready, clean closed mesh.

tiers.note: Scaled to 0.10 m bill to tail. The preview's long generic songbird tail (0.65 units) cut off at the rump and replaced by a short stubby tail (2.8 cm, rounded, 1.1-1.7 cm wide) cocked 50 degrees above level, about 60 degrees above the back line; the body behind the shoulders shortened 0.84x to a ball; the body levelled 8 degrees; generated legs replaced by pinkish-brown procedural legs; small black eye; flight wing cards (short, rounded, barred black on lod0). Colours: dark rufous-brown, darker above, the folded wings and the tail barred black, the belly and flanks barred dark and buff (face bands on lod0), a faint pale buff eyebrow, a paler warm throat, dark bill. Triangles: lod0 1,000 = 675 body + 325 legs, tail, cards and eyes; lod1 400 = 309 + 91; lod2 120 = 91 + 29. GLB 185,524 bytes. lod_m is a suggestion for a 10 cm bird.

rig: bird rig template of the Steller's jay (tools/build_stellersjay.py; drawn with client/src/animalModels.js RIG.stjay's constants): PART BODY 0, LEG_A 1 / LEG_B 2 procedural legs (pivot at the knee), TAIL 3 procedural tail (pivot at the rump), HEAD 6 (head and neck, pivot at the base of the neck), WING_L/R 4/5 and HAND_L/R 9/10 flight cards that collapse into the shoulder on pose; extras.rig {kind 'bird', wing (shoulder), tail (rump), head (neck base), length_m}; no skin
accuracy_notes: Built 2026-11-05 from the Meshy preview, which came back as a generic long-tailed songbird. Reads as a tiny round dark-brown wren with a short cocked tail; the face-band barring on lod0 reads as a fine darker mottling on the flanks and wings rather than crisp bars (the body has about 675 faces), and is absent on lod1/lod2 (plain dark rufous-brown). Still open: the bill is the preview's, a little thick and only faintly decurved; the throat keeps a little of the preview's ruffled sculpting; the neck is short but the head sits a little high; legs are long-ish for a wren. A local birder should check the tail angle and the depth of the brown.
